paper_metadata.title: The Importance of Diffusivity and Partitioning Behavior of Solid Solution Strengthening Elements for the High Temperature Creep Strength of Ni-Base Superalloys

evidence.quote: The Importance of Diffusivity and Partitioning Behavior of Solid Solution Strengthening Elements for the High Temperature Creep Strength of Ni-Base Superalloys
The alloys cast for this work are called Astra2 alloys and their base composition consists of Ni, Al, Co, Cr and Ta.
Single crystalline cylindrical bars of each alloy were produced by a Bridgman vacuum casting unit.

The alloys were solution heat treated at 1573 K (1300 °C) for 12 hours in a vertical furnace ... and subsequently water quenched to dissolve the γ'-phase and intermetallic phases in the interdendritic regions and to homogenize the material.

Further improvement of the creep behavior was observed for the Mo-, W- and especially Re-containing alloys with the lowest creep minimum of 2.67 × 10−7 s−1 (see Figure 6(b)).

The strongest partitioning to the γ-phase and the lowest interdiffusion coefficient of the alloying element, the better the creep resistance. Therefore, the best creep behavior is found for alloys containing high contents of slow-diffusing elements that partition preferably to the γ-phase, particularly Re followed by W and Mo.
The advantage of slow-diffusing elements like Re and W is that they retard dislocation climb at the γ/γ'-interfaces.
